Underfollowed lane emphasizes Rambus and FormFactor as second-order chokepoint candidates tied to HBM controller IP and probe-card/test capacity for AI accelerators and HBM packages. This pass avoids recommendations and treats supplier exposure as research hypotheses unless supported by explicit company disclosures. Expanded the US-listed universe for scarce suppliers tied to custom AI ASIC scaling. The strongest underfollowed chokepoint candidates in this pass sit in memory-interface IP, wafer probe cards, semiconductor test handlers/contactors, and outsourced advanced packaging. Broadcom is retained only as a reference customer/design anchor for custom AI accelerators; the discovery lane focuses on second-order vendors whose AI exposure may appear through test complexity, HBM/interface demand, advanced packaging, or validation bottlenecks rather than direct accelerator sales. Layer 1B expansion for the custom AI ASIC node. Reference lane confirms that custom AI accelerators and AI networking are already a large, visible revenue driver at Broadcom. Underfollowed discovery lane should track enabling chokepoints one or two steps away from the obvious chip designer: memory-interface IP, HBM/AI probe cards, wafer-level burn-in, silicon photonics test, and known-good-die validation.
